first.text: **Owner lines.** Every test is owned by the spec, or specs, of the module it makes sure works. Ownership is written in the test file, never in a spec. Every test file in the repo is JavaScript, so an owner line is a `//` line comment whose whole text, after optional leading whitespace, is `// @spec <project-relative-spec-path>.md`, with one or more spaces between `@spec` and the path and nothing after the path but trailing whitespace. The path is relative to the repo root wherever the test file sits, names an existing Markdown spec under one of the project's declared spec directories, and may hold subdirectories (`// @spec specs/web/web-client-build.md`). Any `//` line comment whose text begins `@spec` is read as an owner line, well formed or not. An `@spec` inside a `/* */` or `/** */` comment is not an owner line and is ignored.

second.text: **The ownership lists.** The command reports (3) each test file with no file-level owner line, naming the file; and (4) each owner line that does not resolve, naming the file, the line number and the text: one naming a path that is not an existing file under any of the project's spec directories, one not in the `// @spec <project-relative-spec-path>.md` form, or one misplaced. With no argument it reports both over the whole tree and exits 0. With a spec path it reports (3) and (4) over the test files that name that spec in an owner line, file-level or block-level, or hold a link line naming one of its statements (that spec's test files), and exits non-zero when (4) holds an entry in one of those files, whichever spec that entry names; (3) alone does not change the exit code. Entries in other files are neither reported nor counted. So a split or rename that retires a spec path leaves every owner line naming it in (4) until it is re-aimed at one of the specs that replaced it.
